questions.topic: Length Of A Shared Default List
questions.stem: A classmate fixes mutable default by using None and creating list inside. Is that correct?

options.text: No, the fix does not work.

questions.explanation: Using None as a default lets the function detect an omitted argument and create a fresh list locally, avoiding the shared-state bug of a mutable default. The sentinel is evaluated once but is not mutated, so each call gets its own list. This is not version-specific or limited to tuples.
